title: Accessible course signup page
goal: Build a responsive course card and signup form with meaningful HTML, native validation, visible keyboard focus, and an evidence-based browser check.
requirements: One clear page heading and one main content area
A course article with a descriptive heading and list
A signup form with connected labels and named controls
A fluid card that does not cause horizontal scrolling
A browser check using Elements, Console, and Network

steps.title: Plan the page and request
steps.task: Create index.html and write what the browser must load.
steps.code:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <title>Course signup</title>
  </head>
  <body></body>
</html>
steps.check: Network shows one successful document request when the file is served.
steps.reason: The document shell gives the browser language, character, viewport, and title information.

steps.title: Add meaningful structure
steps.task: Add header, main, article, headings, and a useful list.

steps.check: The page has one clear h1, and the skip link moves focus to main content.
steps.reason: Landmarks and headings describe the page before visual styling is added.

steps.title: Build the form with native controls
steps.task: Add labeled name and email fields plus a submit button.
steps.code:
Reserve a place

Check the address bar after a valid submission.
steps.check: Clicking either label focuses its field; an empty or invalid email blocks submission.
steps.reason: Native form controls provide names, keyboard behavior, and useful validation before JavaScript.

steps.title: Set predictable boxes
steps.task: Apply border-box and basic readable styles.
steps.check: The card keeps side space and never exceeds 44rem.
steps.reason: Border-box and flexible constraints make the card easier to reason about at different widths.

steps.title: Style controls and focus
steps.task: Use simple class and state selectors without removing focus.
steps.check: Tab reaches every control in order and focus is always visible.
steps.reason: Simple selectors stay maintainable, while focus and validation states remain perceivable.

steps.title: Test at different widths
steps.task: Resize, zoom, and enter long text before adding a breakpoint.
steps.check: The narrow layout remains one column; the wider layout changes only when fields have enough room.
steps.reason: A content-driven breakpoint enhances a working fluid base.

steps.title: Collect browser evidence
steps.task: Use DevTools instead of guessing whether the page works.
steps.check: Elements shows associated labels and winning styles; Console has no errors; Network shows the document response; keyboard and native validation pass.
steps.reason: A repeatable check turns an apparent result into evidence.

steps.title: Rebuild it independently
steps.task: Close the final code and build the same behavior with different content and colors.
steps.check: Meet every acceptance scenario and explain each semantic and layout choice.
steps.reason: Independent transfer is stronger evidence than copying the guided page.
